newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi urged to curb foreign beer, tobacco ventures.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi urged to curb foreign beer, tobacco ventures.

text.p: Vietnam's official army newspaper has called for joint ventures with foreign beer and tobacco firms to be strictly limited and controlled and warned of future dangers if such projects continued to be established.
The commentary, carried Monday in the daily Vietnam News, said that although more investment from abroad was needed, beer and tobacco were not essential in a country where most people were poor.
"If foreign companies are allowed to develop the industry here it will take Vietnam down a dark road which developing countries now try to avoid," the Quan Doi Nhan Dan commentary said.
Demand for beer and tobacco has increased threefold since the early 1990s due to a leap in economic growth and living standards, attracting many foreign companies and heightening local competition.
Quan Doi Nhan Dan said that together, the foreign-invested joint ventures now produce 318 million litres of beer annually, compared with just 70 million in 1993.
Foreign tobacco ventures, whose partners include U.S. giant Philip Morris, produce 20 million packets a year, adding to huge volumes of smuggled cigarettes now competing for Vietnam's market.
Quan Doi Nhan Dan said the government should invest in domestic production of beer and cigarettes to ensure the development of a job-creating industry at home.
It said domestic firms already produce 560 million litres of beer and 2.1 billion packets of cigarettes a year, enough to meet demand.
"In fact, beer and tobacco has been stockpiled since the middle of last year, suggesting an imbalance between supply and demand," it said.

Faced with a rapidly widening trade gap, Hanoi has expressed concern in recent weeks over the growth of consumer goods imports. Although developing export capacity is official policy, some advocate an import substitution and restriction drive.
